        "title": "ARC task-9a9f2d3f: stamp marker shape onto matching zeros",
        "content": "For task-9a9f2d3f, the input is a binary grid (typically 0 plus another color) with a small pattern in a third marker color. Find the marker pattern’s bounding box and its occupied-cell mask. Slide this mask over every in-bounds location of the original grid; whenever every occupied mask position contains 0, recolor those occupied positions to the marker color. Take the union of all hits, preserving all other cells and the original marker. Do not require the mask’s blank positions to match anything. Demonstrated with marker colors 2, 3, and 9; task solved with zero wrong submissions after two demos. Confirmed again on a 25x13 test with marker 5 over background 9: the same rule solved it with no demos or wrong submissions. The marker mask (relative to its 5x4 bounding box, rows top-to-bottom) was `..#.` / `.#..` / `.##.` / `##..` / `..##`; two placements matched. Always test each mask placement against the original grid, then color the union of all matches. Additional validation: this session had a 15x22 grid with background 0/4 and a 5-cell marker stencil `..#` / `.##` / `#.#` (where # is marker color 5). Exact translations over all-zero positions yielded 14 stencil hits (union of 60 new cells); the submission was correct. The same non-rotated, non-reflected translation-only rule held for marker stencils of sizes 4 and 8 in demos.\n\nFurther validation: the current task-9a9f2d3f test was 22x17, with background/noise colors 0 and 6 and six color-5 marker cells. The marker bounding box was 4x3, with occupied offsets (0,0),(1,0),(1,1),(1,2),(2,1),(3,2), i.e. rows `#..` / `###` / `.#.` / `..#`. Matching was checked against the original grid at every in-bounds translation, requiring all six occupied offsets to be 0 while ignoring the blank bbox positions. The 24 hit origins (zero-based) were (0,0),(0,1),(0,3),(1,1),(1,2),(1,4),(3,2),(4,3),(5,1),(6,8),(8,11),(8,12),(9,5),(9,9),(9,11),(9,13),(9,14),(10,8),(10,12),(13,5),(13,14),(15,1),(17,6),(17,11). Recoloring the union of those translated stencil cells to 5 changed 104 cells and solved the instance with zero wrong submissions and no demo requests. This again confirms that all matches are used, including overlapping hits, without requiring bbox blanks to match.\n\nCurrent validation: on a 23x26 grid with 0/1 noise and a 9-cell color-2 stencil in a 4x4 bounding box, scanning the original grid for placements where all nine stencil cells were 0 found 12 origins; coloring the union of all translated stencil cells produced the correct output.       "arc_task_82d6b2bb_complete_repeating_pattern_through_zeros": {
        "id": "arc_task_82d6b2bb_complete_repeating_pattern_through_zeros",
        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC task-82d6b2bb: complete sparse periodic color patterns",
        "content": "Task-82d6b2bb is to complete a periodic color pattern through zeros. Infer the shortest consistent period and its coordinate/orientation from colored cells; fill every cell, not just zeros, using the periodic mapping. For down-right diagonal bands, color depends on d=(c-r) mod p; each observed monochrome band gives the color for that residue. Solved example: p=5 with residues 0→1, 1→3, 2→5, 3→6, 4→9, so every output cell is [1,3,5,6,9][(c-r)%5]. Observations were 1 on d=-5, 3 on d=-4, 9 on d=-1, 6 on d=3, and 5 on d=7. Other verified example: a 14x14 input with down-right bands of colors 1,4,5,8 had p=4 and residue map (c-r)%4: 0→8, 1→5, 2→4, 3→1; output is a full diagonal periodic tile. If stripes are down-left use r+c instead. Horizontal full-row stripes are a special case of periodic completion; infer period and phase from observed row indices, then repeat. Prior demos: rows [0,4,2,9] became [9,4,2,9] (period 3); a stripe sequence with period 7 filled blank rows to match the repeating cycle. Do not assume zeros are background; use all clues to resolve period, axis and phase.\n\nAdditional confirmed anti-diagonal test: on a 9x9 grid, input clue diagonals (indexed by s=r+c) were s=1→7, 3→5, 4→6, 7→8, 10→7, 13→1, 14→8, 16→8. The shortest period consistent with all clues was p=8; residue map s mod 8: 0→8, 1→7, 2→7, 3→5, 4→6, 5→1, 6→8, 7→8. Fill every cell by this map using (r+c) mod p; this solved the instance. More generally, identify which parallel-line coordinate indexes the clues (horizontal rows use r; down-left/anti-diagonals use r+c; down-right diagonals use c-r), choose the shortest period that assigns a single color to each observed residue, then fill all cells with the resulting residue map. The sparse colored tracks encode known values of an underlying periodic pattern; zeros are missing cells, not necessarily output background.",

        "kind": "memory",
        "title": "ARC: periodicize full-width color stripes by stripe count",
        "content": "For ARC grids containing full-width horizontal solid-color stripes separated by background-zero rows: let N be the number of nonzero stripe rows. Treat row indices modulo N as the period. For each residue r, take the color of the input stripe at any row whose index mod N is r; fill every output row with the corresponding color across the full width. This preserves every original stripe and replaces all zero rows. Example task-82d6b2bb: stripes at rows 3=4, 5=7, 10=6 (0-based), N=3, so residues 0,2,1 map to 4,7,6 and output cycles [4,6,7] from row 0.
